truthReview: 2026-09-29: export and import are Settings actions, rehearsed in Electron on macOS with the imported profile opened. A host killed with SIGKILL is rehearsed three ways: idle (the runtime is reclaimed by its launch record), in the middle of an export (named, discarded, exported again) and in the middle of an import (listed, not selectable, imported again). An export is carried between two installations on one Mac with separate user data and credentials, also into an installation running a later Barkpark that descends from the exporting one; no database migration lies between the two versions. The database stopped at once under an open note is rehearsed: the runtime comes back by itself, words typed meanwhile are kept as a retained draft and sent again, and words left unsaved at quit are in a retained draft that the reopened note names; the note puts them back itself in one revision-checked write. A quit in the moment the last key is pressed sends the pending words first; with the database dead they are kept at quit. A stale revision under a concurrent edit is covered by the existing Paper tour, not rehearsed again here. A note with a picture is exported, imported and shown in the imported profile, answered by that profile's runtime while the stored address keeps the exporting port. Five refusals (tampered, truncated, added to, other version, not an export) are rehearsed from Settings and create nothing; an export folder opened in a file manager still imports. The library switch killed under the hold is resumed from the notice and completes; a kill while held with no operation in flight is reopened at launch. A writer whose connection is cut during a drain is not killed by it: the write completes and the hold is reached, so a writer that raises inside the runtime is not produced by any rehearsal. One stall point per operation; the folder picker and the system trash are stubbed in those rehearsals; the Windows reclaim path is written and not rehearsed; no second machine is claimed.
